items.title: Joe LaBarbera interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, July 15, 2021
items.q: I played a lot with Bud Shank.

ctx.x: This may expose my musical tastes but it seems like I hear a lot of contemporary groups now where most people are playing with the time, instead of playing the time. And I wonder if you’ve noticed that kind of thing, maybe in a different fashion, but it almost feels like they’re avoiding being too obvious.

You might have a valid point there, Monk. I haven’t really thought about that too much. I mean I know musicians, like a Joe Lovano for example. Joe plays with the time in a way that makes it very very very fun to play along with. He’ll sit back on the time, you know, he’s not trying to like put it in a metric grid. He’s playing around with the time and you know if you need a comparison for this, the way Basie’s band sits back on the beat, right? So Bud Shank played like that. I played a lot with Bud Shank. He…
Yeah. Right. Imagine trying to fall back with like Billie Holiday or something.
